The implementation of TISUK’s trauma-informed approach within Merrywood Education has had a profound and often life-changing impact on students who attend this setting. By fostering an environment that prioritises compassion, understanding and support for individuals who have experienced trauma, this setting has significantly enhanced student well-being and academic outcomes. Students feel safer, more understood, and better equipped to cope with challenges, leading to improved attendance, engagement, and overall success.
Teachers and staff members are fully equipped to recognize and respond to signs of distress, creating a culture of empathy and empowerment within the school community. This work is supported by a comprehensive therapeutic offer. The ripple effects extend beyond the classroom, positively influencing families and the community at large. In essence, this trauma-informed school doesn’t just educate; it nurtures resilience, fosters healing, and transforms lives. Trauma Informed Schools 2024
Lucy believes that every child can thrive when they feel safe, ambitious and nurtured. She often says, ‘Every child has a right to learn, but not all children learn in the same way’. Lucy’s approach focuses on adapting the environment so children can flourish and reach their full potential.

Unicef Rights Respecting School
Unicef
These rights are based on what a child needs to survive, grow, participate and fulfil their potential. The Rights Respecting School award (RRSA) will help our pupils to grow into confident, caring and responsible young citizens both in school and within the wider community. By learning about their own rights, our pupils also learn about the importance of respecting the rights of others i.e. their responsibilities.
There are four key areas of impact for children at a Rights Respecting school: wellbeing, participation, relationships and self-esteem. These go beyond the school gates, they give children who attend this Rights Respecting school a responsibility that has a positive impact on the whole community.

School of Opportunities
Children are healthier and happier
By promoting the values of respect, dignity and non-discrimination, children’s self-esteem and wellbeing is boosted and they are less likely to suffer from stress. A child who understands their rights understands how they and others should be treated and their sense of self-worth is strengthened.
The Rights Respecting Schools Award gives children a powerful language to use to express themselves and to challenge the way they are treated. They are also able to challenge injustices for other children. Children and young people are empowered to access information that enables them to make informed decisions about their learning, health and wellbeing.
Children have better relationships
In a Rights Respecting school children are treated as equals by their fellow pupils and by the adults in the school. Children are actively involved in strategic decision-making about their learning and the school as well as developing views about their own wellbeing.
Children become active and involved in school life and the wider world
Children build their confidence to make informed decisions. They have a moral framework, based on equality and respect for all that lasts a lifetime, as they grow into engaged, responsible members of society. Children and adults develop an ethos and language of rights and respect around the school. Rights and principles of the Convention are used to put moral situations into perspective and consider rights-respecting solutions – this all has a huge impact on relationships and wellbeing. The children get very involved in raising awareness about social justice issues, both at home and abroad. They become ambassadors for rights and take part in campaigns and activities to help to bring about change.

At Merrywood Education, we are committed to keeping parents and carers informed about school life, important updates, upcoming events and pupil opportunities.
As part of our paperless approach, routine communications, newsletters, letters, notices and school updates are shared electronically through Arbor Parent Portal and the email address we hold on record for parents and carers.
We kindly ask all parents and carers to check their Arbor account regularly and ensure that the school has an up-to-date email address so that important information is received promptly.
We recognise that some families may prefer to receive printed copies of school communications. If you would like to receive hard copies of school letters, newsletters or other routine information, please contact the school office and we will be happy to provide these free of charge.
Thank you for helping us maintain an efficient, environmentally friendly communication system while ensuring that all families continue to receive the information they need.

Curriculum
Merrywood’s Needs Based Curriculum
There are daily lessons in Maths, English and Reading alongside Science, PSHE, SEMH and Human and Social. We understand the importance of emotional and social literacy in developing a child’s character.
For this reason, we follow a Social Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) scheme of work developed by our team of therapists that seeks to empower children to take responsibility for their own mental health. Throughout our curriculum we educate children on relevant topics such as gender inequality, careers aspirations, human rights and social injustice.
We want to inspire our children to develop a love of learning, the self-belief to take risks and the confidence to achieve anything they set their mind to.
Whole School Overview
The Merrywood Early Development Curriculum (Pink Journey)
The Merrywood Early Development Curriculum (Pink Journey) is designed for pupils with Moderate Learning Difficulties (MLD), significant developmental delay and sensory‑cognitive needs. It provides a highly structured, nurturing and ambitious learning experience that reflects each pupil’s developmental stage rather than their chronological age. The curriculum is intentionally designed to ensure that learning is embedded, revisited and strengthened over time, enabling pupils to build secure foundations for future independence.
At the heart of the Pink Pathway is the belief that every child is unique and capable of progress when learning is meaningful, accessible and emotionally safe. The curriculum prioritises active learning, repetition, sensory engagement and the development of new skills through carefully planned experiences. This approach ensures that pupils have the time, space and support needed to consolidate early developmental milestones, while also being challenged to extend their capabilities.
The curriculum is built around the fundamental experiences of early learning, recognising that pupils with MLD often require extended periods of exploration, repetition and reinforcement before skills become secure. By providing a consistent and predictable environment, pupils develop resilience, confidence, capability and self‑assurance. Positive relationships with trusted adults underpin all learning, ensuring that pupils feel psychologically safe and ready to engage.
Merrywood recognises that pupils’ progress is not always linear. Development may occur in small steps, across different domains at different times, and may require repeated exposure to the same concepts. The Pink Pathway is therefore intentionally flexible and responsive. It allows teachers to adapt learning to each pupil’s developmental profile, ensuring that skills are securely embedded before moving forward. This prevents gaps in learning and supports long‑term independence.
Using the Pink Pathway alongside other Merrywood developmental frameworks ensures that pupils experience a coherent, ambitious and personalised curriculum. This combined approach enables pupils to revisit key concepts through multiple modalities, strengthening neural pathways and deepening understanding. Over time, pupils develop the secure knowledge, emotional readiness and practical skills needed to progress into greater independence and access broader areas of learning.
Ultimately, the Pink Pathway ensures that pupils with MLD experience a curriculum that is developmentally appropriate, emotionally attuned and academically ambitious. It supports them to become curious, confident and increasingly independent learners.
The Merrywood Early Education Curriculum (Amber Journey)
The Amber Journey sets out the learning framework beyond the Pink Journey. It is designed for pupils who have begun to establish secure sensory, emotional and early communication foundations and are now well poised to engage with more structured early learning experiences. While still nurturing, highly personalised and emotionally attuned, the Amber Journey introduces greater cognitive challenge, broader learning opportunities and increased expectations for independence. This ensures that pupils continue to feel safe and supported while being gently guided into the next phase of their educational development.
The Amber Journey is firmly rooted in the principles and developmental pathways of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS). By drawing on the EYFS, the curriculum remains developmentally appropriate, play‑based and exploratory, while also being ambitious and carefully sequenced. Learning is designed to reflect how children with SEND acquire knowledge best—through meaningful repetition, rich language experiences, hands‑on exploration and opportunities to practise skills in a variety of contexts. This grounding in the Early Years curriculum ensures that pupils develop the secure foundations required for future academic and wider success.
Central to the Amber Journey is the understanding that pupils’ progress is shaped by their cognitive development, learning needs and EHCP targets. Each pupil’s curriculum is tailored to their developmental profile, ensuring that teaching is precisely matched to their communication needs, social and emotional readiness and preferred learning styles. Learning is broken down into small, achievable steps, allowing pupils to revisit and strengthen skills over time. This approach ensures that pupils experience success, build confidence and develop the resilience needed to engage with increasingly complex learning.
As a progression from the Pink Journey, the Amber Journey moves pupils into more structured early learning experiences while maintaining the nurturing, predictable and emotionally safe environment that underpins all Merrywood practice.
Pupils begin to engage in longer periods of focused activity, follow simple sequences, participate in shared and independent tasks and explore early academic concepts through play and guided learning. This developmental shift reflects pupils’ growing readiness to engage with early literacy, numeracy, communication and problem‑solving, while still benefiting from the sensory‑rich, relational and responsive approaches established in the earlier stage.
The Amber Journey continues to prioritise emotional safety, strong relationships and predictable routines. Pupils are supported through repetition, modelling and multi‑sensory experiences that help them consolidate learning and deepen understanding. Progress is recognised as non‑linear, and pupils are given the time and space needed to revisit concepts until skills are secure. This ensures that learning is embedded rather than rushed, preventing gaps and supporting long‑term independence.
The Merrywood Elementary Curriculum (Magenta Journey)
The Magenta Journey is Merrywood’s curriculum for pupils from Year R to Year 8. It gives pupils a clear and ambitious learning pathway that meets the Independent School Standards. It is built from the EYFS Framework and the National Curriculum, and it is adapted so pupils with SEND, SEMH needs and trauma can access learning in every subject. The curriculum helps pupils build secure knowledge and skills that grow over time and can be used in real‑life situations.
The Magenta Journey places pupils’ emotional safety at the centre of learning. It creates calm routines and strong relationships so pupils feel safe and understood. Teaching is structured and responsive, allowing pupils to revisit key ideas in different ways. Each subject uses repetition, practice and sensory‑rich experiences to help pupils remember important knowledge. Learning is broken into small, achievable steps to support independence.
The Magenta Journey recognises that pupils with SEND and SEMH needs may need more time to learn securely. It uses clear teaching, consistent expectations and purposeful practice to support understanding. Concepts are introduced gradually and revisited often to strengthen long‑term memory. Learning is linked across subjects so pupils can apply knowledge in different contexts. This prevents gaps and ensures pupils master key ideas before moving on.
The Magenta Journey builds learning in steady, manageable steps. It helps pupils develop confidence and resilience as they meet new challenges. Learning is adapted to match each pupil’s developmental stage while keeping expectations high. Emotional readiness, communication and self‑regulation are seen as essential foundations for progress. Personal growth and academic learning are supported together.
The Magenta Journey provides a broad and balanced curriculum across all subjects. It is organsied under specific subject groups which are – computer science, human and social, aesthetic and creative, physical, social, health and relationships sex education and science.
Pupils have opportunities to be creative, develop physical skills and build cultural understanding. Communication and problem‑solving are strengthened through meaningful and connected learning.
Pupils make links across subjects so learning feels joined and purposeful. Practical experiences help pupils use their knowledge in real‑world situations.
The Magenta Journey ensures that pupils with SEND, SEMH needs and trauma histories experience a nurturing and structured curriculum. Teachers adapt and create a curriculum timetable that includes important learning linked to pupils’ SEMH needs.
Teachers work with the senior leadership team to design the most effective and purposeful route so important knowledge is learned securely. The curriculum supports pupils to become curious, capable and confident learners. It builds strong foundations for academic, social and emotional success as pupils move into the next stage of education.

The Merrywood Secondary Curriculum (Lilac, Navy and Green Journey)
The Navy, Lilac and Green curriculums provide our key stage 3 and key stage 4 pupil with a high‑quality academic and vocational options. At each ‘journey’ the curriculum is ambitious, personalised and responsive to pupil’s starting point, aspirations and identified needs within their EHC plans. Our curriculum is designed to ensure that every pupil continues to securely follow an individual learning journey. This approach is aimed to help them to develop the knowledge, skills and independence required for meaningful next steps in education, employment and life.

Merrywood Education educates children with social, emotional and mental health needs (SEMH).
Merrywood Education – School of Opportunities
All children will require a SEMH provision. We support children with historical and current trauma and/or the below:
Self-harming and suicidal ideation
Attachment difficulties
Speech & Language difficulties
Dyslexia or Dyspraxia
Low self-esteem
Speech and language and communication difficulties
Sensory needs
Literacy and numeracy difficulties

Merrywood Criteria & Process
Merrywood Education educates children with social, emotional and mental health needs (SEMH).
All children will require a SEMH provision. We support children with historical and current trauma and/or the below:
Self-harming and suicidal ideation
Attachment difficulties
Speech & Language difficulties
Dyslexia or Dyspraxia
Depression
Lived within a violent and abusive home
Low self-esteem
Display challenging behaviour
Attention and concentration difficulties
Speech and language and communication difficulties
Sensory needs
Literacy and numeracy difficulties
Looked After Child
Parent with Mental Health Needs
Excluded from mainstream education
In addition to this the children will require the following support:
We understand the psychological effects of exclusion and our model has been developed with a trauma informed approach, whilst keeping nurture and boundaries at the core of our daily school lives.
We want every child to feel safe and happy to attend school, primary school is the time when a child should learn, play and build the skills relevant to a successful career educationally and socially.
consultations and referrals
The majority of our consultations are located from London boroughs, Surrey, Kent, Sussex and East Sussex.
